transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

Since the crash about a year and a half ago, even small things on the road make me jump out of my skin, and I can’t bring myself to drive like I used to. I've been avoiding driving so much that my daughter finally stepped in and helped me get this evaluation.
Can you tell me more about what specifically happens when you try to drive or are in a situation that reminds you of the crash, and how that makes you feel?

I go out of my way to stick to back roads and avoid the crash site because just thinking about those roads makes my chest tighten up. When I am in the car, I'm constantly on edge scanning the mirrors, and if a horn honks, my body jerks, my heart races like a drum, and my hands shake for several minutes.
Do you ever experience vivid, intrusive memories or flashbacks of the crash itself, feeling as though you're reliving the event?

Yes, if I hear sirens or see a car speed through a light on TV, I'm suddenly right back in that intersection hearing the crunch of metal and my wife screaming. It feels so real that my hands actually start gripping an imaginary steering wheel, even if I'm just sitting safely in my chair at home.
Have you been avoiding other activities or places besides driving that remind you of the crash, or is it mainly driving and related stimuli that you've been trying to avoid?

It's mostly the driving itself, but because of that, I've had to stop doing a lot of other things I used to love. I stick to small back roads, which means I've been skipping church, my library volunteer shifts, and my grandkids' events because I can't face the highway or the crash site. Just thinking about driving those routes makes my chest tighten up.
Can you describe how your sleep has been since the crash, and have you been having any recurring nightmares about the accident?

Most nights I lie awake for hours staring at the ceiling, replaying the day and worrying about having to drive. When I finally do fall asleep, I wake up two or three times and feel completely exhausted by morning. I don't really have nightmares about the crash, it's just this constant worry and wakefulness that keeps me from resting.
Do you experience excessive worry or anxiety about things other than driving or the crash, such as work, finances, or relationships?
No, I don't really worry about things like work or finances. Almost all of my anxiety and worry is focused on the crash, driving, and feeling like I can't keep my family safe anymore.
Do you often find yourself having difficulty concentrating or feeling irritable, especially when you're not able to avoid thoughts or reminders of the crash?

Yes, I've been very irritable lately and find myself snapping at my wife and daughter over little things, like how they load the dishwasher, which makes me feel ashamed afterward. When I can't avoid reminders of the crash, my nerves are just completely shot and it makes it even harder to stay calm.

When you experience these flashbacks or intrusive memories of the crash, do you feel like you're observing yourself from outside your body or like you're in a daze, disconnected from what's happening around you?

No, I don't ever feel like I'm outside of my body or in a daze when those memories happen. It's more like I'm trapped right back in that driver's seat, feeling all the panic and tension in my own skin.
